- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.4) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition, not from prior trend.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–7 days to reflect momentum.
